newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Forbes aims for Namibia, Botswana listings.
newsitem.headline: Forbes aims for Namibia, Botswana listings.

text.p: South African financial services firm Forbes Group Ltd said on Monday it aimed to list its shares on the Botswanan and Namibian stock exchanges.
The firm, which only listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange last November, said the move was part of the group's plan to expand its interests in Africa.

"We have expanding operations in both Namibia and Botswana and believe that it is appropriate for our shares to be traded on those exchanges," Forbes chief executive Paul Heinamann said in a statement.
The group said it had applied for the listings, but gave no indication of when the shares might start trading.
Forbes has employee benefit consulting operations, a short-term insurance brokerage and a reinsurance arm in Namibia.
In Botswana the firm's operations cover short-term insurance, employee benefit consultancy and actuarial services.
Forbes is the latest in a rash of South African firms to seek secondary listings in Botswana and Namibia.

In the past six months diamond giant De Beers Ltd, car rental firm Avis Holdings Ltd and McCarthy Retail Holdings Ltd have all made the move and greatly boosted the market size of the two tiny bourses.
